item.title: Russian Diesel Deal Confronts Legal Uncertainty
item.description: Oliver Wyman Geostrategy Practice Leader Daniel Tannebaum tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the first Russian diesel shipment under President Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin raises legal and compliance questions while offering limited relief for US fuel prices. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Tannebaum says private companies remain wary of doing business with Russia and warns that uncertainty over US sanctions and technology policy could push foreign governments and businesses toward alternatives to American suppliers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: France Faces New Protests After Week of Violence
item.description: Bloomberg News Paris Deputy Bureau Chief James Regan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that France is deploying tens of thousands of police and shifting protest routes as authorities try to prevent a repeat of last weekend’s violence and looting. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Regan says unrest that began with student demands has broadened into anger over the cost of living, threatening retailers and tourism as France also contends with fiscal and political strains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gershkovich Says Putin Seeks His Terms, Not a Deal
item.description: Wall Street Journal foreign correspondent Evan Gershkovich tells Bloomberg This Weekend that he questions whether the Trump administration fully understands Vladimir Putin’s negotiating tactics after US envoy Steve Witkoff praised the Russian president as a “humanitarian” following Stephen Hubbard’s release. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gershkovich draws on years covering Putin and his own 16 months in Russian custody to argue that the Russian leader remains focused on securing his demands for Ukraine rather than compromising in negotiations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oil Markets Brace for Renewed Iran Fighting
item.description: Bloomberg Economics Chief Emerging Markets Economist Ziad Daoud tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the risk of renewed fighting between the US, Israel and Iran is rising, helping keep oil prices elevated even as energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz recover. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Daoud says the conflict could remain a long-term stalemate, with heightened shipping costs, depleted stockpiles and escalating regional tensions continuing to threaten global energy supplies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Barclays ‘House of Fixed Income’ Pins Future Growth on Equities
item.description: The house built by fixed income is facing an overhaul. Barclays Plc is showing it can do more for clients than trade bonds and arrange debt deals.
item.dc:creator: William Shaw

item.title: Mauritius Carrier Looks at Narrow-Body Jets in Fleet Overhaul
item.description: Mauritius’ state-owned carrier is planning to add single-aisle aircraft and review the planned acquisition of wide-body planes as part of a long-term strategy review.
item.dc:creator: Kamlesh Bhuckory

item.title: Odd Lots: How to Run a Restaurant For Three Decades (Podcast)
item.description: Richard Mott's first foray into hospitality was in the 1980s at the University of Chicago, where he started running a coffee shop in the basement of the business school when he was a grad student. By the time he graduated, he helped grow that single coffee shop into four locations across campus. He's a longtime Chicago-based restaurateur and his farm-to-table restaurant North Pond has been around since the late 1990s. Lately, he's expanded his business to include Spark Shared Kitchen, a catering
item.dc:creator: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway

item.title: Indonesia Begins Trimming Pipeline Gas Exports to Singapore
item.description: Indonesia is reducing natural gas exports to neighboring Singapore as President Prabowo Subianto seeks to shore up domestic supply and strengthen energy security for Southeast Asia’s largest economy.
item.dc:creator: Ben Otto

item.title: Swiss Stocks Are Becoming a Haven From AI Fears Roiling Markets
item.description: Shares of Switzerland’s ultra-defensive big companies are a bright spot in a tumultuous period for European equity markets.
item.dc:creator: Levin Stamm

item.title: Kenya Records Second Ebola Death as Uganda Restricts Transit
item.description: Kenya has reported a second death from Ebola, a 65-year-old woman who was a close family member of the index case, while Uganda said it’s restricting transit for anyone with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of the Congo in an effort to halt the disease spreading.
item.dc:creator: Helen Nyambura

item.title: US LNG Project Developer Funded by Russia’s Novatek, FT Says
item.description: A developer of a liquefied natural gas facility in Alaska received financing from Russia-based Novatek PJSC, an energy giant that is subject to US sanctions, the Financial Times reported.
item.dc:creator: David Stringer

item.title: India Regulator Orders Options Trainer Avadhut Sathe to Refund INR 5.46B
item.description: India’s market regulator has ordered options trader Avadhut Sathe and his trading academy to refund 5.46 billion rupees ($57.5 million) to course participants after finding they provided unregistered investment advice and research services under the guise of stock market education.
item.dc:creator: Samie Modak

item.title: Singapore Expands Haze Investigation to 10 Locally Based Firms
item.description: Singapore expanded its investigation into haze-creating fires in Indonesia that have blanketed the city-state in smog, requesting information from 10 locally registered companies.
item.dc:creator: Lili Pike and Anuradha Raghu

item.title: Iran Plots, Houthi Attacks Spur US Departure Orders in Mideast
item.description: The US has ordered the departure of diplomatic personnel and adjusted staffing at embassies across the Middle East as a result of Iranian efforts to target Americans, as well as threats from Houthi militants in Yemen, according to an American official.
item.dc:creator: Iain Marlow

item.title: Growth, Value Stocks Set for Reshuffle as S&P Adopts New Rules
item.description: Growth and value shares are set for an overhaul after S&P Dow Jones Indices adopted new rules on how to sort equities into the two investment styles.
item.dc:creator: Lu Wang

item.title: Wealth Tax Debate, Midterm Investing, AI Anxiety
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Whitney Tilson, Stansberry Research Editor, and Stephanie Guild, Robinhood CIO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
item.description: Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Notes on Being a Man', 'The Invisible Hand'
item.description: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene discuss their must-read book on this week's edition of "Bloomberg Money." They discuss 'Notes on Being a Man' by Scott Galloway and 'The Invisible Hand of Maria Edgeworth: How a Nineteenth-Century Novelist Taught the World Economics' by Jeanna Smialek. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Family Annual Healthcare Plan Now Costs More Than $28K
item.description: Bloomberg's John Tozzi joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." The annual cost of a US family’s employer-provided healthcare plan reached an average $28,303 this year, 5% more than 2025, according to an annual survey conducted by health policy nonprofit KFF. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Valterra's Forging the Future of Platinum | Chief Financial Officer
item.description: Chief Financial Officers now play a critical role in shaping corporate strategy and positioning organizations to meet future challenges. This episode profiles Valterra Platinum CFO Sayurie Naidoo, who leads the world's largest company producing platinum group metals. One year after its demerger from Anglo American, the South African firm is looking ahead to develop new markets for PGMs as the adoption of battery electric vehicles threatens their primary area of demand. (Source: Bloomberg)
